text:
maria: Quick heads-up — SRE + Product Ops approved an SLO measurement policy change. Two parts: 1) formalized planned-maintenance exclusion tagging, and 2) increase short-term burst allowance from 15% -> 20% for 5m windows during controlled ops. This helps avoid noisy SLO blips during planned rolling capacity ops.

jon: Important. When does this take effect and what do we need to do as operators?

maria: Policy goes live next Monday 00:00 UTC. For any planned maintenance you must: (a) create a maintenance ticket in rjops, (b) mark the maintenance with tag `maintenance:slo_exempt`, and (c) include start/end times in the ticket. SRE will only exclude windows if the ticket + banner exist and the maintenance used the approved operator playbook.

lee: We're also scheduling a small capacity-validation maintenance to exercise the new SLO tagging and burst allowance. Window: Tue 02:00 UTC, duration 15m. Target: rotate 30% of inference warm-standby capacity in us-west-2 to verify SLO accounting and metric tags.

sre-bot: maintenance created: maint-1788000001 | start: 2026-07-14T02:00:00Z | duration: 15m | owner: lee

ops-comm: I'll prepare the status-page banner text and customer PM. Reminder: this is a validation exercise, no expected customer impact but may cause short-lived 5xx tails.

tara: Can we get the exact SLO calculation change spelled out so we can align dashboards?

maria: Yes 10 here's the concise change (ops copy):
```
SLO policy v2.1: Planned maintenance exclusion:
- Requirements to exclude a time window from SLO calculations:
  * maintenance ticket exists in rjops with id and owner
  * metrics during window are tagged with `maintenance:slo_exempt`
  * status page banner or PM sent to affected customers
- Burst allowance: allow +20% error budget consumption for any single 5m window during an approved maintenance.
- Retroactive rule: maints created with backdated tickets within 30 days may be considered for exclusion after review.
```

jon: Who's owning the review for retroactive requests?

maria: SRE+Trust will review retro requests. We have a 72h SLA to respond.

sam: Operator checklist for the Tue run?

lee: Short checklist: 1) create rjops ticket and link here 2) tag metrics: `maintenance:slo_exempt` (we do this via `metrics-tag` helper) 3) run preflight `scripts/capacity_precheck.sh us-west-2` 4) rotate capacity: `rjctl rotate-capacity --region=us-west-2 --pct=30 --reason="slo-policy-validation"` 5) watch alerts + SLO dashboards 6) run post-check script and remove tags.

maria: Abort criteria (if any -> rollback immediately):
- sustained inference 5m error rate > 3%
- p95 latency > baseline + 600ms for >5m
- any loss of control-plane writes

lee: I'll post the exact prometheus expressions for the abort rules in a follow-up.

sre-bot: reminder: maint-1788000001 starts in 48h

ops-comm: Banner draft: "Resilience validation exercise (SRE internal) Tue 02:00 UTC — short window where increased error rates are possible; no planned downtime. Contact support for issues."

tara: For observability: please tag all loadgen runs with `slo-test/1788000001` and keep raw traces. We'll use them for a post-mortem to validate the exclusion logic.

lee: Assigned: lee (owner/run), sam (prechecks), tara (post-run observability), ops-comm (customer comms), maria (SLO policy lead).

jon: One ask: add a one-line note to the SLO dashboard explaining the new burst allowance so oncall isn't surprised.

maria: Done. I'll add the banner and a short doc link: https://redwood.ops/slo-policy/v2.1

lee: Thanks all. If preflight fails we postpone. Otherwise proceed as scheduled. :white_check_mark:
